---
title: Subjects
---

Send subject events to a connected `natsMachine` actor. Use encoded bytes for wire payloads; `parseNatsResult` parses incoming JSON and falls back to a string.

## Subscribe and publish

```ts
const encode = (value: unknown) => new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(value))

actor.send({
  type: 'SUBJECT.SUBSCRIBE',
  config: { subject: 'demo.events', callback: (data) => console.log(data) },
})
actor.send({
  type: 'SUBJECT.PUBLISH',
  subject: 'demo.events',
  payload: encode({ message: 'hello' }),
  onPublishResult: (result) => {
    if (!result.ok) console.error(result.error)
  },
})
```

Subscriptions are keyed by subject; one target subscription is retained per subject. `SUBJECT.UNSUBSCRIBE` removes a subject, and `SUBJECT.UNSUBSCRIBE_ALL` clears the target set. Target configurations survive disconnect/reconnect so the subject manager can restore them on the new connection. Recreate the actor for a completely fresh demo session.

A successful publish callback means the client accepted the publish call. It is not a broker persistence or application-processing acknowledgement.

## Request a reply

```ts
actor.send({
  type: 'SUBJECT.REQUEST',
  subject: 'demo.echo',
  payload: encode({ question: 'hello' }),
  opts: { timeout: 1500 },
  callback: (reply) => console.log('reply', reply),
  onRequestResult: (result) => {
    if (!result.ok) console.error('request failed', result.error)
  },
})
```

Real NATS needs a responder on the subject. The demo sandbox supplies a local responder only for `demo.echo`. A request failure is reported through `onRequestResult`; the reply callback runs on success. `requestHeaders` can asynchronously prepare additional headers before sending. When `opts.timeout` is provided, header preparation and the NATS request share that time budget.

The root obtains current credential headers for each request when configured with a [credential adapter](credentials.qmd). User-provided `requestHeaders` are merged with those headers. Avoid logging authentication headers or placing credentials in the message body.
